\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\footnotesize Trends of the limb salinity contrast \(\Delta S\) split by the frozen-field decomposition: the full trend equals the sum of the salinity-only term (salinity trend with the record-mean velocity), the velocity-only term (velocity trend with the record-mean salinity) and the cross term (full minus the two parts). Intervals in the column of the \(t\) test are 95\% intervals with the bias-corrected effective sample size; those of the sieve bootstrap (10{,}000 resamples, seed 20261104) are given beside them. A dagger marks an effective sample size at its floor of 3, where both interval columns read uninformative. The minimum detectable trend is the half-width of the \(t\) interval. The cross term has no \(t\) interval; its sieve two-sided \(p\) value is given in the last column. Shares are the fractions of the full trend; their sieve intervals are wide where the full trend is small. For the full trend of GLORYS12V1 over 1993 to 2025 the sieve interval excludes zero while the \(t\) interval includes it: the sieve interval is conditional on the stored effective sample size, which lies near its floor of 3, so the verdict follows the bias-corrected \(t\) interval.\end{minipage}
